messages:
Alex: heads-up — after the FP8 rollout to canary today we see a 12% increase in p99 per-token latency for long-form prompts (1k+). rolling back now but wanted to capture data :eyes:
perf-bot: deploy canary fp8_fast_v2 on pool-gamma at 2026-03-18T09:12:30Z (id: d1f4c)
Priya: copying perf logs here. initial traces show an extra 0.8ms per-token on later tokens, not the first few. suggests KV path or kernel fallthrough.
Jeff: do we have kernel counters in the trace? which kernel is being chosen mid-stream?
Sam: quick grep of traces: kernels selected -> [fp8_fast_v2, int8_fallback, fp8_fast_v2, fp8_fast_v2, int4_mixpf]. pattern seems to flip for certain layer shapes.
Maria: that's consistent with selector heuristics: when seq len > 512 we pick a different kernel for large matmuls. maybe calibration made some shapes prefer slower matmul path.
Priya: pasted sampled profiler dump (aggregated per-token):
```
profile_summary:
  tokens: 1024-1536
  avg_token_latency_ms: 3.6
  p95_token_latency_ms: 7.2
  p99_token_latency_ms: 12.1
  kernel_counters:
    fp8_fast_v2: 64.3%
    fp8_slow_v1: 18.9%
    int8_fallback: 13.4%
    int4_mixpf: 3.4%
  kv_cache_hits: 78.2%
  kv_cache_evictions: 0.9%
  batching_window_ms: 8
  avg_batch_size: 6.2
```
Alex: interesting that `fp8_slow_v1` shows up — we thought selector wouldn't pick that for these shapes. any idea why?
Jeff: selector uses runtime heuristics: (seq_len, head_dim, hardware_affinity) + calibration score. calibration scores changed after we re-quantized layer 21-30 last week.
Sam: I pulled a single-request timeline for a long prompt:
```
[t=0ms] recv request
[t=12ms] token0 kernel=fp8_fast_v2
[t=15ms] token1 kernel=fp8_fast_v2
[t=18ms] token2 kernel=int8_fallback (latency +2.5ms)
[t=21ms] token3 kernel=fp8_slow_v1 (latency +3.1ms)
[t=24ms] token4 kernel=fp8_fast_v2
...
```
Priya: that aligns with a selector race: when KV cache populates, shape of subsequent matmuls shrinks and selector re-evaluates, sometimes choosing fallback kernels that are slower but have different memory patterns.
Maria: could KV cache hit transitions cause kernel path changes? maybe cache hit leads to shorter sequence chunks and triggers different kernel family.
Alex: hypothesis: calibration nudged matrix quant params so some layer dims now cross thresholds in selector, causing mid-sequence kernel switches and extra kernel setup overhead.
Jeff: two hypotheses: 1) kernel switch overhead (setup/descriptor) adds ~1-3ms when switching families; 2) fallback kernels have inherently worse per-token throughput on our hardware. both could compound.
Sam: quick A/B: revert calibration for layers 21-30 on canary to see if kernel mix returns to prior distribution. also enable per-token kernel switch counter in telemetry.
perf-bot: telemetry flag enabled: runtime.kern.switch_counter = true on pool-gamma (sample rate 1%)
Priya: small repro script I ran against canary with synthetic 1k prompt. results before revert: fp8_fast_v2 62%, fp8_slow_v1 20%, int8_fallback 14%, avg p99 token=12.1ms. after reverting quant params locally: fp8_fast_v2 89%, fp8_slow_v1 6%, int8_fallback 5%, avg p99 token=7.6ms.
Maria: that's a pretty clear signal. can we automark the calibration that caused this? need a reproducible diff for QA and evals.
Alex: action items:
- Priya: archive calibration snapshot + diff for layers 21-30 (high priority)
- Jeff: add kernel-switch counter to per-token traces and a simple alert if switches per request > 2
- Sam: roll canary revert and collect another 24h of telemetry
- Maria: update selector thresholds so tiny shape deltas don't flip kernels mid-sequence

Priya: doing snapshot now. also adding a small test in calibration pipeline to run a long-sequence per-layer smoke test.
Jeff: I'll add the counter to traces — plan to push a light agent change (no restart) by EOD.
Sam: rolling back canary to fp8_calib_prev now. will monitor. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: rollback complete (d1f4c -> d1f4b). canary pool-gamma now at fp8_calib_prev.
Alex: great. leave this thread for the telemetry results. if p99 improves after 24h we close; otherwise escalate to runtime core.
Maria: one more note — add a KV hit transition metric: fraction of tokens where cache hit status changed mid-turn. might help detect this class of regressions.
Priya: noted, adding that to the telemetry ticket.
Jeff: thanks all. tagging @Sam for follow-up on canary dashboard.
Sam: got it. I'll post a short summary tomorrow with graphs.
Maria: thanks everyone. :heart:
